To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) we propose an algorithm to adaptively stratify the sampling of a function in order to obtain an almost optimal Monte Carlo integration estimate; (ii) we prove that the algorithm is finite-sample optimal, in the sense that the error of the estimate is almost as good as if we would know the function variations everywhere
we provide a finite sample analysis for the adaptive stratified sampling problem in Monte-Carlo integration.

we propose an adaptive stratified sampling scheme that is provably accurate for Monte Carlo integration and we prove a finite-sample analysis of the algorithm that shows that it is almost as accurate as an oracle algorithm that has full knowledge of the function.
In summary, our research is concerned with
adaptive sampling of differentiable functions.
adaptive sampling for Monte Carlo estimation of integrals of differentiable functions, and we show that a sampling algorithm can achieve the same accuracy as an optimal oracle strategy.
adaptive sampling strategies for Monte-Carlo estimation of differentiable functions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed algorithm achieves the optimal convergence rate for a given finite number of evaluations, while being adaptive to the function variations.

we propose a new algorithm that is adaptive in the sense that it samples more often in the oscillatory parts of the function while allocating the samples to be spread on the domain in a low-discrepancy way.

our algorithm can be used to approximate a differentiable function in a way that is almost as accurate as an oracle strategy, and with a number of evaluations of the function that is almost the same as that of a uniform sampling scheme.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide a sampling scheme that is adaptive to the function and has a finite-sample analysis, which is not the case of the standard stratified sampling.
we provide a way to adaptively sample the function in regions that are important, while keeping a good global spread of the samples.
we provide a practical algorithm that is almost optimal, while being simple and efficient.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the algorithm is adaptive in the sense that it does not require a priori knowledge about the function, but only a finite number of samples of the function, and that the algorithm is optimal, in the sense that the number of function evaluations it requires is almost the same as the number of evaluations that an optimal oracle would require.

, when the function is differentiable, the sampling scheme is adaptive to the variations of the derivative of the function (as opposed to the variations of its absolute value), and thus is more efficient in terms of the number of function evaluations.
we can construct adaptive sampling schemes that are both adaptive in the sense that they adapt to the function, and are well-spread on the domain, which are two seemingly conflicting properties.
